semin-durr:2-2.t:
In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.
His saying: {أَن يتركوا}: it fills the place of the two objects of حَسِب according to the majority, and the place of one of them according to al-Akhfash.
His saying: «أنْ يقولوا»: there are several views in it. The first: that it is a badal (substitute) from «أَنْ يُتْرَكوا», an interpreted maṣdar substituted from its like. The second: that it is by dropping the preposition (bi-isqāṭ al-khāfiḍ), which is the bāʾ or the lām, i.e. "for saying" or "because they say". Ibn ʿAṭiyya and Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "If the bāʾ is assumed, it is a ḥāl (circumstantial)." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The meaning with the bāʾ and the lām differs: with the bāʾ it is as you say 'I left Zayd in his state', and with the lām it means 'for the sake of', i.e. did they think that their faith is a cause for being left?" End quote. This is an explanation of meaning; had he explained the i'rab he would have said: "Is their thinking [themselves] left because of their uttering faith?"
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: where is the speech that indicates the content required by the thinking (ḥusbān)? I say: it is in His saying {أَن يتركوا أَن يقولوا: آمَنَّا، وَهُمْ لاَ يُفْتَنُونَ}. That is because its implied form is: 'Did they think their being left unafflicted [was] because of their saying "We believe"?' So the leaving is the first of the two objects of «حَسِب», and 'because of their saying "We believe"' is the khabar (predicate). As for 'unafflicted', it is the complement of the leaving, because it is of the leaving that means rendering (taṣyīr), as in his saying:
3633 - فَتَرَكْتُه جَزَرَ السِّباعِ يَنُشْنَه ... . . . . . . . . . .
(So I left him as slaughter-meat for the beasts of prey, which tear at him…)
Do you not see that, before bringing in the thinking, you can say: 'their being left unafflicted is because of their saying "We believe"', on the [assumption] of 'occurring' and 'settled' before the lām? If you say: «أَنْ يَقُولوا» is the cause of their being left unafflicted, so how can it validly occur as the khabar of a mubtadaʾ? I say: as you say 'his going out is for fear of evil' and 'his beating is for discipline', whereas discipline and fear in your saying 'I went out for fear of evil' and 'I beat him for discipline' were two causes. And you also say: 'I thought his going out was for fear of evil' and 'I supposed his beating was for discipline', making them two objects just as you made them a mubtadaʾ and khabar." [Translator's note: the verse number 3633 here repeats the number already given above (in the entry on al-Qaṣaṣ 68); kept as written.]
The Shaykh said after all this: "It is speech in which there is confusion. He first mentioned that its implied 'unafflicted' is a complement, meaning that it is a ḥāl, because he cast that from His saying {وَهُمْ لاَ يُفْتَنُونَ}, which is a circumstantial clause; then he mentioned that «يُتْركوا» here is of the leaving which is rendering. That is not sound, because the second object of «صيَّر» cannot properly be «لقولِهم», since the implied form would become: 'that they be rendered because of their saying, while they are not afflicted', and this is speech that is not sound. As for the verse he exemplified it with, «جَزَرَ السِّباع» may validly be the second object of تَرَكَ in the sense of صَيَّر, unlike what he assumed in the verse. As for his assuming 'their being left unafflicted is because of their saying [We believe]', on the assumption of 'occurring' and 'settled' before the lām, it is not sound if 'their being left' means 'their being rendered' and 'unafflicted' is a ḥāl, since no mubtadaʾ and khabar can be formed from 'their being left' in the sense of 'their being rendered' and 'their saying', because 'their being left' in the sense of 'their being rendered' needs a second object, since 'unafflicted' for him is a ḥāl, not a second object.
As for his saying 'If you say: «أَنْ يقولوا» …' to the end, it needs extra understanding: his saying that «أَنْ يقولوا» is the cause of their being left is not so, because had it been a cause of it, it would have been attached to it as it is attached to the verb; rather it is a cause of the omitted khabar, which is 'settled' or 'being', and the khabar is other than the mubtadaʾ. Had «لقولِهم» been a cause of the leaving, it would have been part of it and would have needed a khabar. As for his saying 'as you say: his going out is for fear of evil', «لمخافة» is not a cause of the going out but of the omitted khabar, which is 'settled' or 'being'." End quote.
I say: the answer to all that the Shaykh has mentioned is that al-Zamakhsharī only looked to the side of meaning, and his words are sound on that basis. As for his saying "it is not a cause of the going out" and the like, he means in wording; as for meaning, it is certainly a cause of it. And were it not for fear of departing from the purpose… [Translator's note: the sentence breaks off here in the source; translated as written.]

semin-durr:3-3.t:
His saying: {فَلَيَعْلَمَنَّ الله الذين صَدَقُواْ}: the generality read it with fatḥa on the yāʾ, the imperfect of «عَلِم» which is transitive to one object — so they said. There is a difficulty in it that has been raised more than once: when it is transitive to one object it means عَرَفَ ("to come to know"), and this meaning may not be attributed to the Creator, the Exalted, because it requires prior ignorance, and because it relates only to the essence, not to the states in which it is.
ʿAlī and Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad read it with ḍamma on the yāʾ, the imperfect of أَعْلَم. It may be from عَلِم meaning عَرَفَ; when the hamza of transfer was brought, it gave it another object, which was omitted. Then this object may be the first, i.e. "Allah will surely make known to people the truthful, and make known to them the liars", i.e. by a renown by which these are distinguished from those; or it may be the second, i.e. "He will surely make known to these their stations, and to those their stations in the Hereafter". It may also be from العلامة, which is the mark (sīmiyāʾ), in which case it is transitive only to one object, i.e. "We will surely make for them a mark by which they are known". Al-Zuhrī read the first like the well-known reading and the second like the irregular one.

semin-durr:4-4.t:
His saying: {أم حَسِبَ}: this «أم» is disjunctive (munqaṭiʿa), and so it is estimated as بل plus the hamza according to the majority; the digression (iḍrāb) is a transition, not a cancellation. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "«أم» is the counterpart of the alif in His saying «أَحَسِبَ», as though He, Mighty and Majestic, made both parties acknowledge: He made the believers acknowledge [their thinking that they] will not be tried, and the disbelievers that they will outstrip Allah's punishment." The Shaykh said: "It is not a counterpart, since had it been so it would be conjunctive (muttaṣila), and it cannot be conjunctive for the lack of two conditions. The first: what follows it is not a single word or what is equivalent to one. The second: there is nothing here that is answered by one of two or more things."
Al-Zamakhsharī permitted this «حَسِبَ» to be transitive to two objects, making «أنَّ» and what falls within its scope fill their place, as in His saying {أَمْ حَسِبْتُمْ أَن تَدْخُلُواْ الجنة} [al-Baqara: 214]; or to be transitive to one, on the view that it contains the meaning of «قَدَّر» ("to reckon"). However, implication (taḍmīn) is not regular.
His saying: {سَآءَ مَا يَحْكُمُونَ}: «ساء» may mean بِئْس, and then «ما» is either a relative meaning الذي, with «يَحْكمون» its ṣila (relative clause), and it is the fāʿil (agent) of «ساء», the one specified for blame being omitted, i.e. "their judgement". Or «ما» may be a tamyīz (specification), «يَحْكُمون» its adjective, and the agent a latent pronoun explained by «ما», the one specified also omitted. Or «ما» may be maṣdariyya (infinitival), which is the view of Ibn Kaysān; on this the tamyīz is omitted and the interpreted maṣdar is the one specified for blame, i.e. "evil as a judgement is their judgement". The ruling on «ما» when joined to «بِئْسَ» has preceded fully in al-Baqara. «ساء» may also mean قَبُح ("is ugly"), in which case «ما» may be maṣdariyya, or mean الذي, or be an indefinite qualified noun. «يَحْكمون» was used rather than "they judged" either to point out that this is their habit, or because it stands in place of the past for the sake of the verse-ending.

semin-durr:5-5.t: His saying: {مَن كَانَ}: it may be conditional or relative, the fāʾ [then being] because of its resemblance to the conditional. The apparent view is that this is not the apodosis, because Allah's term is coming inevitably without being restricted by a condition; rather the apodosis is omitted, i.e. "let him do righteous work and associate no one in the worship of his Lord", as He has stated explicitly.

semin-durr:7-7.t:
His saying: {والذين آمَنُواْ}: it may be nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), the khabar (predicate) being the omitted oath clause and its answer, i.e. "By Allah, We will surely expiate". It may be accusative by an implied verb by way of occupation (ishtighāl), i.e. "We will surely free those who believe from their misdeeds".
His saying: {أَحْسَنَ الذي كَانُواْ يَعْمَلُونَ}: it has been said: with a muḍāf omitted, i.e. "the reward of the best". What is meant by «أَحْسَن» here is mere description. It has been said: so that it does not follow that their reward for the good is passed over in silence. This is nothing, because it is a fortiori: if He rewards them for the best, He rewards them for what is below it; so it is of pointing to the lower through the higher. His saying: {والذين آمَنُواْ}: the nominative as a mubtadaʾ and the accusative by way of ishtighāl are both possible in it.

semin-durr:8-8.t:
His saying: {حُسْناً}: there are several views in it. The first: that it is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "a good enjoining" — either by way of hyperbole, being made goodness itself, or with a muḍāf omitted, i.e. "possessing goodness". The second: that it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "There is figurative usage in that; the original is: 'We enjoined on man goodness in his conduct with his parents'. Similar to this is the poet's saying:
3634 - عَجِبْتُ مِنْ دَهْماءَ إذ تَشْكُوْنا ... ومِنْ أبي دَهْماءَ إذ يُوصِيْنا
خيراً بنا كأنَّنا جافُونا ...
(I marvelled at Dahmāʾ when she complained of us, and at Dahmāʾ's father when he enjoined good to us concerning her, as though we had been harsh to her.)
and like it the saying of al-Ḥuṭayʾa:
3635 - وَصَّيْتُ مِنْ بَرَّةَ قلباً حُرَّاً ... بالكَلْبِ خيراً والحَماةِ شَرَّاً
(I enjoined upon a noble heart from Barra good towards the dog and evil towards the mother-in-law.)
On this the original is: 'We enjoined him with goodness in the matter of his parents'; then the parents were put in the genitive with the bāʾ, and «حُسْناً» became accusative; likewise the two verses. The bāʾ in the verse and the two verses in this case is locative." [Translator's note: the source numbers these verses «363 - 4-» and «363 - 5-», i.e. 3634 and 3635.]
The third: that «بوالديه» is the second object, and «حُسْناً» is accusative by an implied verb, i.e. "he does good, a doing of good", so it is an emphatic maṣdar. So it has been said; and there is room for consideration in it, because the governor of an emphatic [maṣdar] is not omitted. The fourth: that it is a direct object by implication (taḍmīn), i.e. "We obliged him [to] goodness". The fifth: that it is by dropping the preposition, i.e. "with goodness"; the author of al-Taḥrīr expressed that as "cutting off" (qaṭʿ). The sixth: that some of the Kufans estimated it as "We enjoined on man that he do good to his parents"; in this there is omission of «أنْ» and its ṣila with retention of what it governs, which is not permissible according to the Basrans. The seventh: that the implied form is "We enjoined on him giving his parents goodness"; in this there is omission of the maṣdar with retention of what it governs, which is not permissible. The eighth: that it is accusative in the same way as «زيداً» in your saying to someone you see preparing to strike: «زيداً», i.e. "strike Zayd!"; the implied form here is "show them goodness" or "do goodness to them". Al-Zamakhsharī said these two.
ʿĪsā and al-Jaḥdarī read «حَسَناً» with two fatḥas; they are two dialectal forms, like البُخْل and البَخَل. That has preceded at the beginning of al-Baqara.

semin-durr:10-10.t: His saying: {لَيَقُولُنَّ}: the generality read it with ḍamma on the lām, attributing the verb to a plural pronoun, construing according to the meaning of «مَنْ» after it was construed according to its wording. Abū Muʿādh the grammarian reported that it was read «لَيَقُولَنَّ» with fatḥa, likewise continuing in regard to its wording. The reading of the generality is better because of His saying «إنَّا كُنَّا».

semin-durr:12-12.t:
His saying: {وَلْنَحْمِلْ}: an imperative with the meaning of a statement. Al-Ḥasan and ʿĪsā read it with kasra on the lām of the imperative, which is the dialect of the Ḥijāz. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "This was the saying of the chieftains of Quraysh; they used to say to those of them who believed: 'Neither we nor you will be resurrected; and if perhaps that should be (fa-in ʿasā kāna dhālika), then we will bear [your sins].'" The Shaykh said: "It is a non-Arab construction, in respect of introducing the conditional particle onto «عسى», which is inflexible (jāmida), using it without a noun or a predicate, and making كان follow it."
The generality read «خطاياكُمْ» as a broken plural. Dāwūd ibn Abī Hind [read] «مِنْ خَطِيْئاتهم» as a sound plural; from him also «خَطيئتِهم» in the singular, meaning the genus — this resembles the two readings of {وَأَحَاطَتْ بِهِ خطيائته} [al-Baqara: 81] and «خطيئاته». From him also «خَطَئِهم»; it has been said: with fatḥa on the ṭāʾ and kasra on the yāʾ, meaning with kasra on the hamza that is close to yāʾ, because of its being lightened "between-between" (bayna bayna).
And «مِنْ شيء» is the object of «حامِلين», and «مِنْ خطاياهم» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from it; since it precedes it, it became accusative as a ḥāl.

semin-durr:14-14.t: His saying: {أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ}: accusative as an adverbial (mafʿūl fīhi). {إِلاَّ خَمْسِينَ عَاماً} is accusative as an exception. There is disagreement over the occurrence of exception from number nouns, and those who forbid it have an answer regarding this verse. A fine subtle point has been observed here: He varied between the tamyīz (specification) of the two numbers, saying in the first «سَنَة» and in the second «عاماً», so that the wording would not be heavy. Then He assigned the word «عام» to the fifty, to indicate that Allah's Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, once relieved of them, remained in a good time; the Arabs express fertility by العام and drought by السَّنَة.

semin-durr:15-15.t: His saying: {وَجَعَلْنَاهَآ}, i.e. the punishment, or the flood, or the like.

semin-durr:16-16.t:
His saying: {وَإِبْرَاهِيمَ}: the generality read it in the accusative, conjoined to «نوحاً», or by an implied "remember", or conjoined to the hāʾ of «أَنْجَيْناه». Al-Nakhaʿī, Abū Jaʿfar and Abū Ḥanīfa [read] «وإبراهيمُ» in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), the khabar (predicate) being implied, i.e. "and among the messengers is Abraham".
His saying: «إذ قالَ» is a badal (substitute) from «إبراهيمَ», a substitute of inclusion (badal ishtimāl).

semin-durr:17-17.t:
His saying: {وَتَخْلُقُونَ}: the generality [read it] with fatḥa on the tāʾ, sukūn on the khāʾ and sukūn on the lām [Translator's note: as written in the source; in the common reading the lām carries a ḍamma], the imperfect of خَلَقَ, with «إفكاً» with kasra on the hamza and sukūn on the fāʾ, i.e. "and you fabricate lies" or "you carve idols". ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, Zayd ibn ʿAlī, al-Sulamī and Qatāda [read it] with fatḥa on the khāʾ and on the lām, doubled; it is the imperfect of «تَخَلَّقَ», the original being تَتَخَلَّقُوْن with two tāʾs, one of which was deleted, as in تَنزَّلُ and the like. It is also narrated from Zayd ibn ʿAlī «تُخَلِّقُوْن», with ḍamma on the tāʾ and a doubled lām, the imperfect of the doubled خَلَّق.
Ibn al-Zubayr and Fuḍayl ibn Zurqān read «أَفِكاً», with fatḥa on the hamza and kasra on the fāʾ; it is a maṣdar like الكَذِب in meaning and pattern. Al-Zamakhsharī permitted two views for الإِفْك with kasra and sukūn. The first: that it is lightened from الأَفِك with fatḥa and kasra, like الكِذْب and اللِّعْب, whose originals are الكَذِب and اللَّعِب. [The second:] that it is an adjective of the pattern فِعْل, i.e. "a false creation", i.e. "possessing falsehood". I say: his assuming a muḍāf before إفك while making it an adjective is unnecessary; it would only be needed if he made it a maṣdar.
His saying: «رِزْقاً»: it may be accusative as a maṣdar, its governor being «لا يَمْلِكون», because it is in its sense. On the principles of the Kufans, the original may be "they are not able to provide you a provision", so «أَنْ يَرْزُقوكم» is the object of «يَمْلكون». It may also mean "what is provided", so it is accusative as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

semin-durr:19-19.t:
His saying: {يَرَوْاْ كَيْفَ}: the two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] and Abū Bakr read it in the second person, as Abraham's addressing his people with that; the rest in the third person, referring back to the denying nations.
His saying: «كيف يُبْدِئُ»: the generality read it with ḍamma on the yāʾ, from أَبْدَأَ. Al-Zubayrī, ʿĪsā and Abū ʿAmr — with a disagreement [in transmission] from him — [read] «يَبْدَأُ», the imperfect of بدأ; its past has been stated explicitly here where He said {كَيْفَ بَدَأَ الخلق} [al-ʿAnkabūt: 20]. Al-Zuhrī read «كيف بَدا» with a plain alif; it is an irregular lightening, its regular form being "between-between" (bayna bayna). In irregularity it is like his saying:
3636 - . . . . . . . . . . ... فَارْعَيْ فَزارةُ لا هَناكِ المَرْتَعُ
(…so graze, Fazāra — may the pasture not be wholesome for you!)

semin-durr:20-20.t: His saying: {النشأة}: Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read «النَّشاءةَ» with lengthening here, in al-Najm and in al-Wāqiʿa; the rest with the short form and sukūn on the shīn. They are two dialectal forms, like الرَّأْفة and الرَّآفة. Their being accusative is as a maṣdar with its additional letters dropped, the original being الإِنشاءة; or by omission of the governor, i.e. "He originates, so they originate an origination". It is written with an alif, and that strengthens the reading with lengthening.

semin-durr:22-22.t:
His saying: {وَلاَ فِي السمآء}: on the supposition that they were in it, as in His saying {إِنِ استطعتم أَن تَنفُذُواْ مِنْ أَقْطَارِ السماوات} [al-Raḥmān: 33], i.e. on the supposition that they were in it. Ibn Zayd and al-Farrāʾ said: "Its meaning is: nor whoever is in the heaven, i.e. can escape [Him] if he disobeys" — meaning that "whoever is in the heavens" is conjoined to «أنتم», with the implied "if he disobeys". Al-Farrāʾ said: "This is one of the obscure points of Arabic." I say: this is according to his principle, since he permits the omission of the nominal relative while its ṣila remains. He recited:
3637 - أمَن يهْجُو رسولَ الله منكُمْ ... ويَنْصُرُه ويَمْدَحُه سَواءُ
(Is the one of you who satirizes the Messenger of Allah, and [the one who] supports him and praises him, equal?)
More remote than that is whoever assumed two omitted relatives, i.e. "You cannot escape [from] whoever is on the earth of humans and jinn, nor whoever is in the heaven of the angels; so how could you escape their Creator?" On the view of the majority, the object is omitted, i.e. "you are not able to escape", i.e. to evade what Allah wills for you.
His saying: «ثم يُعيدُه» and {ثُمَّ الله يُنشِىءُ} are both resumptive, of Allah the Exalted's informing; so the first is not included within the scope of the seeing, nor the second within the scope of the looking.
[Translator's note: the final paragraph, on «ثم يعيده» and «ثم الله ينشئ», pertains to verses 19–20, though it appears under this entry in the source.]

semin-durr:24-24.t: His saying: {فَمَا كَانَ جَوَابَ قَوْمِهِ}: the generality read it in the accusative; al-Ḥasan and Sālim al-Afṭas in the nominative. The verification of this has preceded.

semin-durr:25-25.t:
His saying: {إِنَّمَا اتخذتم}: in this «ما» there are three views. The first: that it is a relative meaning الذي, the referent pronoun being omitted — it is the first object — and «أَوْثاناً» the second object. The khabar (predicate) is «مَوَدَّةُ» in the reading of those who put it in the nominative, as will come; the implied form is: "that which you have taken as idols is affection", i.e. "a matter of affection", or it was made affection itself. And it is omitted in the reading of those who put «مَوَدَّةَ» in the accusative, i.e. "that which you have taken as idols for the sake of affection will not benefit you" or "will be against you", indicated by His saying {ثُمَّ يَوْمَ القيامة يَكْفُرُ بَعْضُكُمْ بِبَعْضٍ}.
The second: that «ما» is made restrictive-cancelling (kāffa) and «أوثاناً» a direct object. The taking here is transitive to one object, or to two, the second being {مِّن دُونِ الله}. Whoever puts «مودةُ» in the nominative makes it the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "it is affection", i.e. "possessing affection", or it was made affection itself by way of hyperbole; the clause is then an adjective of «أَوْثاناً» or resumptive. Whoever puts it in the accusative makes it a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), or [accusative] by an implied "I mean".
The third: that «ما» is made maṣdariyya (infinitival). In that case a muḍāf may be assumed in the first part, i.e. "the cause of your taking idols is affection", for those who read «مودةُ» in the nominative; or it may not be assumed, the taking itself being made the affection by way of hyperbole. In the reading of those who put it in the accusative, the khabar is omitted, as passed in the first view.
Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr and al-Kisāʾī read «مودةُ» in the nominative without tanwīn and «بَيْنِكم» in the genitive. Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir and Abū Bakr [read] «مودةً» in the accusative with tanwīn and «بينَكم» in the accusative. Ḥamza and Ḥafṣ [read] «مودةَ» in the accusative without tanwīn and «بَيْنِكم» in the genitive. The nominative has been dealt with. The accusative too has been dealt with, with two views; a third view is possible, which is that it be made a second object by way of hyperbole, the annexation being by latitude with the adverbial, as in their saying:
3638 - يا سارِقَ الليلةِ أهلَ الدارِ ...
(O you who rob the people of the house on this night [lit. "O robber of the night, the people of the house"].)
Whoever put it in the accusative did so according to its original [status]. It is transmitted from ʿĀṣim that he read «مودةُ» in the nominative without tanwīn and «بينَكم» in the accusative; it has been explained on the basis of annexing «مودةُ» to the adverbial, which was only made indeclinable because it is annexed to something non-declinable, like the reading {لَقَد تَّقَطَّعَ بَيْنَكُمْ} [al-Anʿām: 94] with fatḥa if we make «بينَكم» the agent.
As for «في الحياة», there are [several views] in it. The first: that it and «بينَكم» are both attached to «مودَّة» when it has tanwīn; it is permissible for both to be attached to one governor because they differ. The second: that they are both attached to something omitted, as two adjectives of «مودَّة». The third: that «بَيْنَكم» is attached to «مودَّة» and «في الحياة» is an adjective of «مودة»; the reverse is not permissible, lest it entail the governance of a maṣdar that has been qualified. The difference between it and the first is that in the first the maṣdar governed it before being qualified, while here it governed it after being qualified.
However, Ibn ʿAṭiyya and others permitted that, as though they allowed latitude with the adverbial; so this is a fourth view.
The fifth: that «في الحياة» is attached to «بينَكم» itself, because it has the sense of the verb, since the implied form is "your coming together and your union". The sixth: that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «بينَكم» itself. The seventh: that «بينَكم» is an adjective of «مودة» and «في الحياة» a ḥāl from the pronoun latent in it. The eighth: that «في الحياة» is attached to «اتَّخذتُمْ», on the view that «ما» is kāffa and «مودة» accusative. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Lest it lead to separation between the relative and what is in the ṣila by the khabar."

semin-durr:28-28.t:
His saying: {وَلُوطاً}: like His saying {وَإِبْرَاهِيمَ إِذْ قَالَ} [al-ʿAnkabūt: 16].
His saying: «ما سَبَقكم»: it may be resumptive, as an answer to someone who asked about that, or circumstantial, i.e. "originating it".

semin-durr:33-33.t:
His saying: {وَلَمَّآ أَن جَآءَتْ}: its parallel has preceded, except that here «أَنْ» has been added, which is regular, for emphasis.
His saying: «إنَّا مُنَجُّوك»: regarding the kāf and the like there are two doctrines. The doctrine of Sībawayh: that it is in the position of a genitive; on this there are two views on the accusative of «وأهلَكَ»: an implied verb, or conjunction to the position. The doctrine of al-Akhfash and Hishām: that it is in the position of an accusative, and the tanwīn and the nūn were dropped because of the strong attachment of the pronoun.
The two readings with the light and doubled [jīm] in «لنُنَجِّيَنَّه» and «مُنَجُّوك» have preceded in al-Ḥijr.

semin-durr:34-34.t: «مُنْزِلون» was read both light and doubled. Ibn Muḥayṣin read «رُجْزاً» with ḍamma on the rāʾ. Al-Aʿmash and Abū Ḥaywa [read] «يَفْسِقون» with kasra.

semin-durr:35-35.t:
His saying: {تَّرَكْنَا مِنْهَآ آيَةً}: there are two views in it. The first: that part of it remains, and it is a sign that remains to this day. The second: that «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida); al-Farrāʾ inclined to this, i.e. "We left it as a sign", as in his saying:
3639 - أمْهَرْت مِنْها جُبَّة وتَيْسا ...
(I gave her as dowry a cloak and a he-goat.)
i.e. "I gave her as dowry". This comes on the view of al-Akhfash. [Translator's note: the source prints the verse number as «363 - 9-», i.e. 3639.]

semin-durr:36-36.t: His saying: {وإلى مَدْيَنَ}, i.e. "and We sent", or "We dispatched", to Madyan their brother. And «شُعَيباً» is a badal (substitute), or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition), or [accusative] by an implied "I mean".

semin-durr:38-38.t:
His saying: {وَعَاداً وَثَمُودَاْ}: accusative by an implied «أَهْلَكْنا» ("We destroyed"), or conjoined to the object of «فأَخَذْتُهم», or to the object of {فَتَنَّا} [al-ʿAnkabūt: 3] at the beginning of the sūra — this is the view of al-Kisāʾī, and there is great remoteness in it. The tanwīn of Thamūd and its absence have preceded in Hūd.
Ibn Waththāb read «وعادٍ وثمودٍ» in the genitive, conjoined to «مَدْيَنَ», conjoined merely for indication, even though it does not follow that «شعيباً» was sent to them both; and it is not so.
His saying: {وَقَد تَّبَيَّنَ لَكُم}, i.e. what befell them. Al-Aʿmash read «مساكنُهم» in the nominative as the agent, with «مِنْ» omitted.

semin-durr:39-39.t: His saying: {وَقَارُونَ}: conjoined to «عاداً وثمودَ», or to the object of «فَصَدَّهم», or by an implied "remember".

semin-durr:40-40.t:
His saying: {فَكُلاًّ}: accusative by «أَخَذْنا». «بذَنْبه», i.e. because of, or accompanied by, his sin.
His saying: «مَنْ أَغْرَقْناه»: its referent pronoun is omitted because of its resemblance to a verse-ending. [Translator's note: the verse reads «مَنْ أَغْرَقْنا»; the source cites it with the pronoun.]

semin-durr:41-41.t:
His saying: {العنكبوت}: well known. Its nūn is radical, and the wāw and the tāʾ are additional, as proved by their saying in the plural عناكِب and in the diminutive عُنَيْكِب. It is treated as masculine and feminine; of the feminine is His saying «اتَّخَذَتْ», and of the masculine his saying:
3640 - على هَطَّالِهم منهمْ بيوتٌ ... كأنَّ العنكبوتَ هو ابْتَناها
(On their [mount] Haṭṭāl they have houses, as though the spider [masc.] had built them.)
This is regular in generic nouns: they are treated as masculine and feminine.
His saying: {لَوْ كَانُواْ يَعْلَمُونَ}: its answer is omitted, i.e. "they would not have taken [as patrons] one for whom these parables are struck because of his insignificance". The object of the knowing cannot be of the type of His saying {وَإِنَّ أَوْهَنَ البيوت}, because everyone knows that; rather its object is implied, of the type the context indicates, i.e. "if they knew that this is their parable".

semin-durr:42-42.t: His saying: {مَا يَدْعُونَ}: Abū ʿAmr and ʿĀṣim read it with the yāʾ of the third person, and the rest in the second person. «ما» may be a relative, accusative by «يَعْلَم», i.e. "He knows those whom they call upon, and knows their states", with «منْ شيء» a maṣdar. It may be interrogative, in which case two views are possible: that it, together with what governs it, is parenthetical between His saying «يَعْلَمُ» and His saying {وَهُوَ العزيز الحكيم}, as though it were said "what thing do they call upon besides Him?"; and the second: that it suspends (muʿalliqa) «يَعْلَم», so it is in the position of an accusative by it — al-Fārisī went to this. It may be negating, with «مِنْ» in «من شيء» redundant in the direct object, as though it were said: "they do not call upon besides Him anything that deserves to be called a thing"; the view in it then is that the clause is parenthetical, like the first of the two views of the interrogative. And it may be maṣdariyya (infinitival); Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "and شيء is a maṣdar". There is room for consideration in this, since the implied form would become "and He knows your calling upon anything of calling".

semin-durr:43-43.t: His saying: {نَضْرِبُهَا}: it may be the khabar (predicate) of «تلك», with «الأمثالُ» a naʿt (adjective), badal (substitute) or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition); or «الأمثالُ» may be the khabar and «نَضْرِبُها» a ḥāl (circumstantial); or it may be a second khabar.

semin-durr:46-46.t: His saying: {إِلاَّ الذين ظَلَمُواْ}: a conjoined exception (muttaṣil). There are two meanings in it. The first: except the wrongdoers — do not dispute with them at all, but contend with them by the sword. The second: dispute with them in a way other than the best, i.e. be harsh with them as they were harsh with you. Ibn ʿAbbās read «ألا», a particle of alerting, i.e. "so dispute with them".

semin-durr:48-48.t:
His saying: {مِن كِتَابٍ}: the object of «تَتْلُو», with «مِنْ» redundant (zāʾida). «مِنْ قبلِه» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «كتاب», or attached to «تَتْلو» itself.
His saying: «إذاً لارتابَ»: an answer and a requital, i.e. had you recited a book before the Qurʾān, or been one who writes, the falsifiers would have doubted.

semin-durr:49-49.t: His saying: {بَلْ هُوَ آيَاتٌ}: Qatāda read «آيةٌ» in the singular.

semin-durr:50-50.t: His saying: {آيَاتٌ}: the two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī], Ibn Kathīr and Abū Bakr read «آيةٌ» in the singular, because most of what comes in the Qurʾān is so. The rest [read] «آياتٌ» in the plural, because after it comes {قُلْ إِنَّمَا الآيات} in the plural by consensus, and the script admits it.

semin-durr:51-51.t: His saying: {أَنَّآ أَنزَلْنَا}: the fāʿil (agent) of «يَكْفِهم».

semin-durr:55-55.t:
His saying: {وَيِقُولُ}: the Kufans and Nāfiʿ read it with the yāʾ of the third person, i.e. Allah the Exalted or the angel. The rest of the Seven [read it] with the nūn of majesty, for Allah the Exalted, or for the company of angels.
Abū al-Barahsam [read it] with the upper-dotted tāʾ, i.e. Hell, as in His saying {وَتَقُولُ هَلْ مِن مَّزِيدٍ} [Qāf: 30]. ʿAbdallāh and Ibn Abī ʿAbla [read] «ويُقال» in the passive.

semin-durr:56-56.t: His saying: {فاعبدون}: al-Zamakhsharī made it the answer of an implied condition, and made the fronting of the object a compensation for its omission, while also conveying restriction. The Shaykh's dispute with him over its parallel has preceded.

semin-durr:57-57.t: His saying: {ثُمَّ إِلَيْنَا تُرْجَعُونَ}: Abū Bakr read it in the third person, and likewise in al-Rūm in His saying {ثُمَّ إِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ} [al-Rūm: 11]; Abū ʿAmr agreed with him in al-Rūm only. The rest [read] in the second person in both. It was also read «يَرْجِعُون» in the active voice.

semin-durr:58-58.t:
His saying: {والذين آمَنُواْ}: the two well-known views are possible in it: the mubtadaʾ (subject) and ishtighāl (occupation). The two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] read [لَنُثْوِيَنَّهم] with a three-dotted thāʾ with sukūn after the nūn and a yāʾ with fatḥa after the wāw, from الثَّواء, which is residing. The rest [read لَنُبَوِّئَنَّهم] with a one-dotted bāʾ with fatḥa after the nūn and a hamza with fatḥa after the wāw, from المَباءة, which is lodging. [Translator's note: in both cases the source's "after the wāw" refers to the doubled/second radical position as written; translated as written.] On the first reading, «غُرفاً» is either a direct object by making «أَثْوَى» contain the meaning of «أنزل», so it is transitive to two objects — because ثوى is intransitive and the hamza gave it transitivity to one — or by likening the specific adverbial of place to the vague one, as in His saying {لأَقْعُدَنَّ لَهُمْ صِرَاطَكَ} [al-Aʿrāf: 16], or by dropping the preposition by latitude, i.e. "in chambers".
As for the second reading, it is a second object, because «بَوَّأ» is transitive to two objects; the Exalted said {تُبَوِّىءُ المؤمنين مَقَاعِدَ} [Āl ʿImrān: 121]; and it is also made transitive with the lām; the Exalted said {وَإِذْ بَوَّأْنَا لإِبْرَاهِيمَ} [al-Ḥajj: 26]. It was also read «لَنُثَوِّيَنَّهم», doubled, with the three-dotted thāʾ, made transitive by doubling just as it was made transitive by the hamza. And «تَجْرِي» is an adjective of «غُرَفاً».

semin-durr:59-59.t: His saying: {الذين صَبَرُواْ}: the genitive, the accusative and the nominative are possible in it, like its parallels that have preceded.

semin-durr:60-60.t: His saying: {وَكَأَيِّن مِّن دَآبَّةٍ}: Abū al-Baqāʾ permitted two views in «كَأَيِّن». The first: that it is a mubtadaʾ (subject), «لا تحملُ» its adjective, «اللَّهُ يَرْزُقها» its khabar (predicate), and «مِنْ دابَّةٍ» an explication (tabyīn). The second: that it is in the position of an accusative by an implied verb explained by «يَرْزُقها», which is estimated after «كَأَيِّنْ» — meaning because it has the front position in speech. There is room for consideration in the second, because a condition of the explaining [verb] is that it be capable of governing, and this explaining [verb] does not govern, because if it governed it would take the place of the first, but it cannot take its place, since when the khabar is a verb that puts a singular pronoun in the nominative, its fronting before the mubtadaʾ is forbidden. If you want to know this rule, see Sūrat Hūd at His saying {أَلاَ يَوْمَ يَأْتِيهِمْ لَيْسَ مَصْرُوفاً} [Hūd: 8].

semin-durr:64-64.t:
His saying: {الحيوان}: Abū al-Baqāʾ and others assumed a muḍāf before the mubtadaʾ, i.e. "and the life of the Abode of the Hereafter". They only assumed that so that the mubtadaʾ and the khabar would correspond; hyperbole is better.
The wāw of «الحيوان» is from a yāʾ according to Sībawayh and his followers; it was only changed to a wāw irregularly, and likewise in «حَيْوَة» as a proper name. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Lest it be confused with the dual", meaning if one said حَيَيان. He said: "It was not changed to an alif, despite its having a vowel and what precedes it having a fatḥa, lest one of the two alifs be deleted." Others than Sībawayh took that at face value, so for them the final radical of الحياة is a wāw. Sībawayh has no proof in «حَيِي», because whenever what precedes a wāw has a kasra it is changed to a yāʾ, e.g. غُزِي, دُعِي and رَضِيَ.
His saying: {لَوْ كَانُواْ يَعْلَمُونَ}, i.e. had they known that it is the [true] life, they would not have preferred this world to it.

semin-durr:65-65.t: His saying: {فَإِذَا رَكِبُواْ}: al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: to what is His saying {فَإِذَا رَكِبُواْ فِي الفلك} connected? I say: to something omitted, indicated by what He described them with and set forth of their affair. Its meaning: they are as they were described, of associating partners and obstinacy; then when they embark…"

semin-durr:66-66.t:
His saying: {لِيَكْفُرُواْ}: it may be the lām of kay (purpose), which is the apparent view, or the lām of the imperative.
His saying: «ولِيَتَمَتَّعوا»: Abū ʿAmr, Ibn ʿĀmir, ʿĀṣim and Warsh read it with kasra [on the lām], which admits the two preceding possibilities; the rest with sukūn, which is apparent in the imperative. If one holds the first lām to be for the imperative, he has conjoined an imperative to its like; if one holds it to be for causation, he has conjoined speech to speech.
ʿAbdallāh read {فَتَمَتَّعُواْ فَسَوْفَ تَعلَمُونَ}, and Abū al-ʿĀliya «فيُمَتَّعوا» with the lower-dotted yāʾ in the passive.

semin-durr:67-67.t: His saying: {أفبالباطل يُؤْمِنُونَ}: the generality read «يُؤْمنون» and «يكفرون» with the yāʾ of the third person; al-Ḥasan and al-Sulamī with the tāʾ of address in both.

semin-durr:68-68.t:
His saying: {أَلَيْسَ فِي جَهَنَّمَ}: an interrogative of affirmation (istifhām taqrīr), as in his saying:
3641 - ألَسْتُمْ خيرَ مَنْ رَكِبَ المطايا ... وأندى العالمين بطونَ راحِ
(Are you not the best of those who ride mounts, and the most generous of all people in the palms of the hand?)
[Translator's note: the source prints the verse number as «364 - 1-», i.e. 3641.]

semin-durr:69-69.t:
His saying: {والذين جَاهَدُواْ}: what was possible in His saying {والذين آمَنُواْ} [al-ʿAnkabūt: 7] at the beginning of the sūra is possible in it. In it is a refutation of Thaʿlab, since he claimed that an oath clause does not occur as the khabar (predicate) of a mubtadaʾ (subject).
His saying: «لَمع المحسنين»: of putting the overt noun in place of the pronoun, to show their nobility.
